subquestions.prompt_template: The first term of an arithmetic series is {a}. The common difference is {d} and the series contains {n} terms. Calculate the sum of this series.
The original arithmetic series is extended to {n2} terms. The sum of these {n2} terms is {S_n2}. Using sigma notation, write down an equation for the sum of the terms added to the original series.
subquestions.derive: S_n = n/2*(2a+(n-1)d); S_n2 = n2/2*(2a+(n2-1)d); c = a - d; n_plus_1 = n + 1; S_n2_minus_S_n = S_n2 - S_n
steps: Sum of terms added: S_{n2} - S_{n} = {S_n2_minus_S_n}

subquestions.prompt_template: The sequence of the first differences of a quadratic pattern is: {d1}; {d2}; {d3}; ... If T_{N} of this quadratic pattern is {T_N}, calculate the value of T_{N_minus_1}.
subquestions.derive: d2 = d1 + step; d3 = d1 + 2*step; N_minus_1 = N - 1; D_at_N_minus_1 = d1 + (N - 2)*step; T_N_minus_1 = T_N - D_at_N_minus_1
steps: First difference at position N-1: D_{N_minus_1} = d1 + (N-2)(step)

subquestions.prompt_template: If it is further given that the third term of the quadratic pattern is {T3}, determine the general term, T_n, of the quadratic pattern.
subquestions.derive: a = step / 2; b = d1 - (3*step)/2; c = T3 - 9*a - 3*b
steps: First differences: D_n = a(2n-1) + b. When n=1: {d1} = a + b  =>  b = {b}.
